configure-projected-volume-storage.md.summary: This page explains how to use a projected volume to mount several existing volume sources (like secrets, configMaps, etc.) into a shared directory within a Kubernetes Pod.

configure-redis-using-configmap.md.title: Configuring Redis using a ConfigMap
configure-redis-using-configmap.md.summary: This page demonstrates how to configure Redis using a ConfigMap, showing the process of creating a ConfigMap with Redis configuration values, mounting a Redis Pod to use it, and verifying the configuration via Redis CLI.

configure-runasusername.md.title: Configure RunAsUserName for Windows pods and containers
configure-runasusername.md.summary: This guide explains how to set the `runAsUserName` setting for Windows pods and containers using Kubernetes manifests, allowing pods to run as a specific user on Windows nodes.

configure-service-account.md.title: Configure Service Accounts for Pods
configure-service-account.md.summary: This guide explains how to configure ServiceAccounts for Pods in Kubernetes, detailing how Pods authenticate as ServiceAccounts, how to opt out of API credential automounting, and the automatic revocation of credentials when Pods are deleted.

configure-upgrade-etcd.md.title: Operating etcd clusters for Kubernetes
configure-upgrade-etcd.md.summary: This guide explains how to deploy, manage, and restore etcd clusters for Kubernetes, emphasizing leader-based architecture, odd-numbered member requirements, and resource isolation for stable production deployments.

configure-volume-storage.md.title: Configure a Pod to Use a Volume for Storage
configure-volume-storage.md.summary: This page explains how to configure a Kubernetes Pod to use a Volume for persistent storage, specifically using an emptyDir volume that persists the container's filesystem state even after the container terminates and restarts.

connect-applications-service.md.title: Connecting Applications with Services
connect-applications-service.md.summary: This guide explains the Kubernetes networking model where pods communicate directly without explicit host-to-pod mappings, allowing services to be exposed across the cluster. It details how to create a Service to abstract pods and define their unique IPs, ensuring reliable service discovery even after pod failures.

connecting-frontend-backend.md.title: Connect a Frontend to a Backend Using Services
connecting-frontend-backend.md.summary: This guide demonstrates how to create a frontend microservice and a backend microservice using Kubernetes, deploying a hello greeter backend and exposing it via a LoadBalancer service.

container-env-variables.md.title: Container Environment Variables
container-env-variables.md.summary: Container environment variables are name=value pairs defining useful information for running containers within pods, including file system details and cluster resources.

container-environment.md.title: Container Environment
container-environment.md.summary: This page describes the Kubernetes container environment, detailing filesystems (images and volumes), container information (hostname, pod name), and cluster services (services with dedicated IPs and DNS support).

container-lifecycle-hooks.md.title: Container Lifecycle Hooks
container-lifecycle-hooks.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes manages Containers using the hook framework to run code triggered by events during their lifecycle, including PostStart, PreStop, and StopSignal hooks.

container-runtime.md.title: Container Runtime
container-runtime.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes' container runtime, detailing how it manages container execution and lifecycle within the Kubernetes environment, including supported runtimes like containerd and cri-o.

container-runtimes.md.title: Container Runtimes
container-runtimes.md.summary: This page outlines how to install and configure container runtimes (like containerd, CRI-O, Docker, and Mirantis) on Linux nodes within a Kubernetes cluster, emphasizing the need for a CRI-compliant runtime and managing cgroup drivers for resource management.

container.md.title: Container
container.md.summary: This page explains containers as lightweight, portable executable images that decouple applications from host infrastructure, enabling easier deployment and scaling across cloud or OS environments.

containerd.md.title: containerd
containerd.md.summary: A lightweight container runtime built for simplicity and portability, handling image fetching, execution, and networking.

containers.md.title: Containers
containers.md.summary: This page explains containers, container images, and their use in operations. It details how containers decouple applications from host infrastructure, are stateless and immutable, and how RuntimeClass allows different pods to run with different container runtime settings.

contributor.md.title: Contributor
contributor.md.summary: A role where individuals donate code, documentation, or time to help the Kubernetes project or community, including PRs, issues, SIG participation, and organizing events.

control-plane-flags.md.title: Customizing components with the kubeadm API
control-plane-flags.md.summary: This page explains how to customize control plane components like APIServer, ControllerManager, and Scheduler using the kubeadm API, including flags in ClusterConfiguration and patches per-node.

control-plane-node-communication.md.title: Communication between Nodes and the Control Plane
control-plane-node-communication.md.summary: This document details the secure communication paths between the Kubernetes API server and nodes, including the hub-and-spoke architecture where API requests terminate at the kubelet. It specifies that the API server uses HTTPS (port 443) with client certificates for authentication, and pods can connect securely via service accounts. The control plane communicates with nodes over the same secure port, enabling untrusted network deployments.

control-plane.md.title: Control Plane
control-plane.md.summary: This page describes the container orchestration layer that exposes APIs for defining, deploying, and managing container lifecycles, composed of components like etcd, API Server, and Scheduler.

controller-manager-leader-migration.md.title: Migrate Replicated Control Plane To Use Cloud Controller Manager
controller-manager-leader-migration.md.summary: This guide details the process of migrating replicated control plane components from the kube-controller-manager to the cloud-controller-manager, enabling leader migration for HA clusters.

controller.md.title: Controllers
controller.md.summary: This page explains the Controllers pattern in robotics and automation, detailing how controllers track Kubernetes resources, manage state via API server interactions, and handle direct control of external systems.

controllers.md.title: Kubernetes Workload Management
controllers.md.summary: Kubernetes provides declarative APIs for managing workloads, including Deployments for stateless apps, StatefulSets for persistent pods with identity, and DaemonSets for node-specific drivers. It automates Pod replacement and manages cluster networking, essential for container orchestration.

controlling-access.md.title: Controlling Access to the Kubernetes API
controlling-access.md.summary: This page explains how to control access to the Kubernetes API, detailing TLS security, authentication steps, and authorization processes for both human users and service accounts.

coordinated-leader-election.md.title: Coordinated Leader Election
coordinated-leader-election.md.summary: Kubernetes enables leader selection via coordinated leader election to satisfy version skew constraints. This feature allows control plane components (kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler) to automatically elect a leader using the Lease API, which acts as a distributed lock to prevent race conditions during cluster upgrades.

coredns.md.title: Using CoreDNS for Service Discovery
coredns.md.summary: This page outlines the upgrade process and installation steps for CoreDNS, including manual deployment instructions and the kubeadm tool for automatic retention. It also details tuning options and provides links to documentation on scaling and the Kubernetes plugin.

cpu-constraint-namespace.md.title: Configure Minimum and Maximum CPU Constraints for a Namespace
cpu-constraint-namespace.md.summary: This page explains how to set Kubernetes limits on CPU resources for containers and Pods within a namespace, ensuring pods meet minimum and maximum CPU requirements.

cpu-default-namespace.md.title: Configure Default CPU Requests and Limits for a Namespace
cpu-default-namespace.md.summary: This page explains how to set default CPU requests and limits for a Kubernetes namespace, including how pods without explicit limits default to 0.5 request and 1 limit, and how to override these defaults with custom manifests.

cpu-management-policies.md.title: Control CPU Management Policies on the Node
cpu-management-policies.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes manages CPU policies for pods on nodes, detailing default CFS-based scheduling, alternative policies for high-latency workloads, and Windows-specific CPU Manager features.

create-cluster-kubeadm.md.title: Creating a cluster with kubeadm
create-cluster-kubeadm.md.summary: This guide explains how to create a Kubernetes cluster using the kubeadm tool, covering prerequisites like Linux OS and RAM, objectives of installing a control-plane node and a pod network, and installation steps for both new and existing hosts.

create-daemon-set.md.title: Building a Basic DaemonSet
create-daemon-set.md.summary: This page demonstrates how to create a Kubernetes DaemonSet that runs a Pod on every node, using an init container to log host paths and a pause container to keep the Pod running.

create-external-load-balancer.md.title: Create an External Load Balancer
create-external-load-balancer.md.summary: This page explains how to create an external load balancer using YAML manifests or kubectl, including configuration for LoadBalancer type, ingress configuration, and how to find the load balancer's IP address.

create-hostprocess-pod.md.title: Windows HostProcess Containers
create-hostprocess-pod.md.summary: This guide explains how Windows HostProcess containers enable networked workloads on Windows nodes without requiring dedicated proxies, allowing administrators to deploy plugins and services while reducing privilege requirements.

cri-o.md.title: CRI-O
cri-o.md.summary: CRI-O is a Kubernetes tool that enables running OCI-compliant container runtimes via Kubernetes, allowing pods to use compatible runtimes and fetch OCI images from remote registries.

cri.md.title: Container Runtime Interface (CRI) API Reference
cri.md.summary: This page explains the CRI plugin interface used by kubelet to connect to various container runtimes, including v1 API support requirements, upgrade handling, and streaming RPCs for large-scale container lists.

crictl.md.title: Debugging Kubernetes nodes with crictl
crictl.md.summary: This page explains how to use crictl, a command-line interface for CRI-compatible container runtimes, to inspect and debug container runtimes and applications on a Kubernetes node.
